description: ocsp.rs lines 186-188 (and 290-292): when `now > nextUpdate` (stale response) or `nextUpdate` is absent, the code returns `Err(OcspStatusUnknown)`. This is semantically wrong: a stale OCSP response is not equivalent to the responder saying 'I don't know this certificate'. The CRL checker correctly distinguishes these: CrlExpired is a separate error. OcspStatusUnknown implies a live responder actively returned unknown status, which is a hard-fail signal meaning 'stop trusting this cert'. A stale response should signal 'I cannot confirm freshness' (equivalent to CrlExpired) — a different action for callers (e.g., fetch a fresh response) vs. 'the responder says unknown' (revoke or hard-fail). As written, an expired OCSP response and a live 'unknown' status are indistinguishable to callers, preventing retry logic or better diagnostics. Suggested fix: add an `OcspExpired` error variant (mirroring `CrlExpired`) and return it from the staleness checks; reserve `OcspStatusUnknown` strictly for `CertStatus::Unknown` and the serial-not-found case.
title: P0: OCSP expired nextUpdate returns OcspStatusUnknown, not a distinct error
